correctness.rationale: The intrinsic projection of an entry normal has norm sqrt(1-1/(2m)); an adjacent Monge normal has norm 2. Center feasibility is exactly the coordinate floors and adjacent row-difference gaps. Pairing ordered differences gives sum |d_j| >= r floor(m^2/2). Every equality case has constant gaps and minimal rowwise positive/negative decomposition; parity forces theta=0 for odd m and theta in [-1,1] for even m. Feasible examples attain the resulting upper bound. Tangent counts and segment length follow by checking active irredundant facets. Standalone checker passed 12661 exact/numerical tests (m<=50 symbolic and m<=18 independent full LP); finite checks do not supply the proof.

value.rationale: The exact inradius and all maximum-ball centers form a complete intrinsic Euclidean invariant for a natural infinite family of non-square Monge polytopes of unbounded dimension. There is a genuine parity jump between uniqueness and a positive-length center segment, plus a sharp tangent-facet jump at its endpoints. Neither facet/volume descriptions nor the square-only metric theorem provide this rectangular geometric classification. No general arbitrary-rectangle theorem is claimed.
